original_question: Find a combinatorial interpretation for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.
target_in_paper: Problem 33 in Section 2 (Problems of 2025), which the notebook explicitly attributes to [Bren2024, Prob. 1.10]: find a combinatorial interpretation for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact target problem and keeps the focus on ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, rather than drifting to the neighboring questions on combinatorial invariance (Problem 31) or on realizing every Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial as P_{e,w}(q) (Problem 32). ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))
missing_details: It does not state the quantifiers: the problem ranges over every Coxeter system (W,S) and every pair u,v in W with u ≤ v in the Bruhat order. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

It does not specify that the object to interpret is the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q)=P^{∅,-1}_{u,v}(q)=P^{∅,q}_{u,v}(q), which lies in Z[q]. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

It does not make explicit what counts as the desired interpretation: Brenti asks for an explicit combinatorial construction of a set M(u,v) and a statistic s:M(u,v)→N such that P_{u,v}(q)=Σ_{a∈M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

It does not record the paper-faithful restriction that a merely recursive realization is not the intended endpoint here; Brenti notes that Deodhar gives a recursive construction of such an M(u,v), but that this is not generally regarded as the sought combinatorial interpretation. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

It does not distinguish the ordinary problem from the separate parabolic combinatorial-interpretation problem mentioned only afterward; to stay faithful to Problem 33, the refined version should remain with the ordinary polynomials P_{u,v}(q). ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
refined_question: Given a Coxeter system (W,S) and elements u,v∈W with u≤v in the Bruhat order, construct, in an explicit combinatorial way, a set M(u,v) and a statistic s:M(u,v)→N such that the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q)=P^{∅,-1}_{u,v}(q)=P^{∅,q}_{u,v}(q)∈Z[q] satisfies P_{u,v}(q)=Σ_{a∈M(u,v)} q^{s(a)} for every such pair u≤v. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
justification: The draft matches Problem 33 verbatim in the notebook. The sharpest stand-alone refinement comes from the source that Problem 33 itself cites, namely Brenti’s Problem 1.10, because Brenti is where the intended meaning of combinatorial interpretation is spelled out via the data M(u,v), s, and equation (1.4). Problems 31 and 32 are different neighboring Kazhdan–Lusztig questions, and Brenti’s later remarks on parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials are presented as an additional direction rather than as the same target, so they should not be folded into the refined question. ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))
